cost: Per unknown word: memoised recursion over (string, depth) with R rules (~80), each cut O(len) and <= 9 stem candidates; dictionary probes O(1) expected; worst case O(R^DEPTH) bounded by distinct suffixes of the word in the memo. Rules parsed once (OnceLock).
description: Derived words: a form the dictionary does not know read as a known open-class word with productive affixes (prefix, suffix, inflection on a derived word, British spelling variant); rules are seed data (```derive blocks), spelling by join.
forward: parse reads ```derive lines (prefix/suffix/inflect/variant with options after=, except=, block=, start=, nostart=, part=) into Rules in seed order. go(w, depth) memoised: a dictionary word of an open class with >=4 letters (>=5 when UD lacks it) is a base with its dictionary tags; else each rule cuts its affix: variant rewrites the British ending and recurses; prefix (optional hyphen) recurses on the rest (shortest stem, start/nostart, except, block by rival prefix + rest in the dictionary) and keeps the stem tags of its classes (part= maps participles); suffix/inflection try stems(rest) and keep a stem s only when join(s, affix) contains w, s ends in after= and not in except=, no rival block suffix makes a dictionary word, the stem base-class matches, and an inflection only on a derived stem. Analyses sorted by (steps, prefix-final). a word of the lexicon extension is also a base below the form (its classes added to a dictionary word's). analyses() is empty for dictionary and extension words (derivations() still explains an extension word) and Early Modern endings (morph::ending_verb). tags() unions the tags of analyses of the best rank; hint() is tags unless EN_DERIVE_TAGS=0.
inverse: compose(stem, rule) = prefix + stem (or with hyphen), the British ending for a variant, join(stem, affix) for suffix/inflection: every step word is in compose(step.stem, step.rule) (test steps_compose_back). The reverse of go is many-valued: one form has several analyses (downsampled = down- + sampled = downsample + -ed); the analysis does not recover meaning or the lexical bracketing, only compatible stems.

No analysis for: a dictionary word; a non-ASCII-lowercase/hyphen string; a bottom word of a closed class, a proper noun, shorter than 4 letters, or of 4 letters known only from AGID; a prefix rest shorter than the rule minimum or with a second hyphen; a spelling join does not give back (misspellings happyness, noticable, arguement, basicly); a blocked rival (unpossible, readible, inpossible, foregetting); an inflection on a dictionary word; more than 4 steps; an EModE ending on a known verb (biteth).
limitations: The dictionary (AGID) lacks many non-comparable adjectives (directional, objective, lateral only as NN); the lexicon extension (en-lexext) adds their JJ reading to a base, so bidirectional is JJ; a base neither has keeps its dictionary tags
Rare false analyses of names and misspellings remain (poppler = popple + -er, spooner, unlogical)
Compounds (treebank) are out of scope; irregular derivatives (grammatical, artificial) come from the lexicon extension, not from rules
No meaning is derived; glosses are explanations only
state: Compiled seed texts, OnceLock rule table, built-in dictionary; EN_DERIVE_TAGS read once.
